notes.title: Dev Blog: A Look Into the Story
notes.notes:
[p]Crafting a compelling narrative for a video game is a unique and intricate dance, a blend of traditional storytelling and interactive design. For [i]Sky of Tides[/i], we embarked on a journey to create a world that not only captivated players with its visuals but also resonated deeply with its story. Today, we're delving into the heart of that process, exploring how we wove the narrative fabric of numen9.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35734802/4591e169d3893900f266b0c7fae4f38c09a86a74.png"][/img]
One of the most rewarding aspects of creating a narrative video game is the ability to tell a story through the player's own journey of discovery. In [i]Sky of Tides[/i], players explore diverse environments, uncovering objects and clues that reveal the world's lore, its characters' motivations, and the central conflict. This approach allowed us to layer depth and detail into the narrative as they explored, enriching the player's experience in a way that’s unique to interactive storytelling.[/p][p]Unlike film, TV, or novels, where the story is often delivered through dialogue or narration, games prioritize player agency. The player [i]is[/i] the main character; their choices drive the narrative forward. This interactive element allows for non-linear storytelling, multiple endings, and a deeply personal connection to the story. [i]Sky of Tides[/i] presented a fascinating case study, as we simultaneously developed the game, an animated series, and a collection of short stories, each offering a distinct perspective on the world of numen9.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35734802/8c53443646c110e8a6c992f6b19343b049769500.png"][/img]
Our story development process began with the core question: Who is the player inhabiting? From there, we considered the game's mechanics and user experience. The story needed to organically integrate with gameplay, reaching a climax and conclusion that felt earned. In [i]Sky of Tides[/i], given the setting of a broken planet with oceans hovering in the sky and two factions vying for power, the theme of balance emerged as a central pillar. We then worked hard to align the narrative with the character stat mechanics. This thematic unity was crucial in shaping the final form of the story, creating a cohesive and meaningful experience.[/p][p]Creating memorable characters in a game requires a delicate balance of surprise, motivation, and depth. We wanted characters that felt both relatable and intriguing, individuals with distinct personalities and compelling goals. The Syndicate Agent Streak Tybo’s relentless pursuit of Rin, or the enigmatic wild man in the bleached relics, Loaj, are examples of characters designed to pique curiosity and invite exploration.[/p][p]Great video game dialogue is concise, impactful, and action-driven. It needs to propel the story forward, never feeling like a drag. Drawing inspiration from stage plays and small-budget films, we focused on crafting dialogue that revealed character and advanced the plot in meaningful ways. The dialogue choice mechanic further engages players, allowing them to shape conversations and explore alternate responses that feel authentic to the characters.[/p][p]The story of [i]Sky of Tides[/i] evolved significantly throughout production. Initially, we drafted a linear narrative, akin to a film script. As game mechanics and gameplay elements were refined, we adapted the story to fit the interactive format, creating scripts that could be integrated into the game engine. The theme of balance, which became central to the gameplay, also influenced the narrative, leading to a revised ending that felt more thematically resonant.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35734802/515d84cdb9f2a18ca0a00e0f426768b13b54fe97.png"][/img]
The collaborative nature of game development was crucial in shaping the story. Writers, designers, and developers worked closely to ensure that the narrative and gameplay elements were seamlessly integrated. This iterative process allowed us to refine the story, ensuring that it resonated with players on a deeper level.[/p][p]Creating [i]Sky of Tides[/i] was a unique endeavour, particularly as we developed the game and animated series simultaneously. This allowed us to explore the world from multiple perspectives, enriching the overall narrative and creating a more immersive cross-platform experience. The interconnected stories of Rin and the characters that inhabit numen9 all add up to a rich and detailed tapestry.[/p][p]Ultimately, we aimed to craft a story that felt both personal and expansive, a journey of discovery that resonated with players on an emotional level. We hope you'll find yourselves immersed in the world of numen9, uncovering its secrets and forging your own path through the fractured skies.[/p][p]– The Sky of Tides Team.[/p]

notes.title: Dev Blog: More Than One Way to Win: Understanding Sky of Tides' 32 Endings
notes.notes:
[p]Excitement is building for Sky of Tides, and the 32 endings are a big talking point! Let’s clarify what that means for your journey through numen9.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35734802/04b4a75338cc91c25d9753499cea125650e72335.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Some might worry that 32 completely different branches would water down the narrative, but that’s not how Sky of Tides works. Instead, your choices and actions shape Rin’s five core stats: [b]compassion, intelligence, courage, luck, and humor.[/b] Each stat is tied to a major outcome in the game, and the fate of one of the key characters Rin forms a bond with over the nine episodes of Sky of Tides. Reaching stat thresholds for each stat determines how each story concludes.[/p][p]This gets to the main difference between Sky of Tides’ core mechanic and those of other RPGs. numen9 is already a world totally out of balance–with planetoids hovering in space, the oceans floating in the sky, and two factions vying for control on the brink of all-out war. [/p][p]The typical min-maxing approach where players double down on one character trait doesn’t quite fit when everything is already at an extreme, and that’s why the game rewards your ability to reach a threshold with [i]each[/i] of your character traits, and restore an element of balance. [/p][p]Each trait is tied to a major outcome in the game. The "32 endings" come from the [b]combinations[/b] of these individual character outcomes. With five key characters and varying resolutions for each based on your stat development, the possibilities multiply. It’s an intricate web of interconnected stories, rather than wildly divergent and unrelated paths.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35734802/cf9bd32b18b6863276a20b5d591229993dc6e398.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The goal is to give players a satisfying experience no matter where they end up statwise, but also allow a way to play again to see a different outcome with characters they feel particularly close to. [/p][p]And if you can achieve balance and unlock the “true” ending of the game, we have a reward. We’ll throw in the Sky of Tides: Atla animated series, which loads right inside the game. [/p][p]Sky of Tides offers a deeply personal experience where your choices directly influence the fates of those around you. For players who value narrative and relationships, this system provides a compelling and rewarding journey. The 32 potential combinations of outcomes highlight the depth and impact of your choices. [/p][p]We look forward to you discovering all the ways your story can unfold![/p]

notes.title: Sky of Tides Dev Blog 04/29/25
notes.notes:
Welcome back, explorers of numen9!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35734802/3b87d2307f850b847e270658dc371f4e9f9389e0.png[/img]

Stepping into the fractured world of Sky of Tides is like wandering through a living painting. Every vista, character, and detail is a deliberate stroke, sparking wonder and mystery. Today, we’re pulling back the curtain to reveal the artistic vision behind numen9.
The visual identity of numen9 weaves together sci-fi futurism and grounded familiarity. Think Borderlands—hand-drawn textures give our 3D environments a bold, comic-book edge. But the real spark came from the story: oceans rising into the sky, leaving a shattered landscape studded with vibrant crystals. These became symbols of unity and division, driving the art’s narrative.
Lina Skorbach kicked things off with early world designs, setting numen9’s unique tone. Concept artist Daxiong (illustrator for Justice League and Star Wars comics) shaped characters like Rin, brought to life in 3D by our wonderful modelers (Nick, Victor, Sangho). Creative director Judith Cheung tied it all together with detailed references that kept the team on track.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35734802/967f41d1ddd543f254db2a7d90d74fe03922004d.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35734802/a72e51753a347542d39ac758816e42ec940fb3da.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35734802/bbb50c5c2d94f81c5ee68ff5e5c5458c86733712.png[/img]

We leaned into a vibrant, colorful palette to match the story’s hopeful, humorous vibe—numen9 is inviting, not oppressive. Balancing danger and awe, ancient ruins and sleek tech, was a tightrope walk. And then there’s the floating oceans: we experimented with rendering tricks to make water feel omnipresent yet never suffocating.
Game art isn’t just eye candy—it sets the emotional stage while wrestling with tech limits. Using Unity, we optimized assets and iterated endlessly based on playtests. The nine planetoids of numen9, once whole, mirror real-world fractures, but their vivid, interconnected design whispers hope. Cutscenes in 2D add a cinematic twist, deepening your bond with the story.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35734802/9667f169471b736ad97220f3a39e6d6bbeec965a.png[/img]

Our goal? A world dripping with mystery, begging you to explore its secrets and piece together its lore. The art of numen9 is a team effort—a collision of creativity and vision. We can’t wait for you to dive in and lose yourself in it.

notes.title: Sky of Tides Offers a New Take on the Genre with Balance at its Core!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

Did you know that Sky of Tides has been compared to other recent, popular narrative RPG adventures but with a key difference? Although the game has [b]32 endings[/b], balance (not min-max) leads to the true ending. Outcomes in the game are tied to the player’s ability to reach thresholds in each of the five character stat categories — [b]compassion, intelligence, courage, luck, and humor[/b]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35734802/b680cea149f28ac951fcfa6a77e13e72c0d8f62b.jpg[/img]

Achieving balance unlocks the game's true ending and leads to a special reward: During the initial release and for a limited time, players who attain the true ending will unlock the entire [b]five-episode exclusive animated series[/b] set in the same world, [b]right inside the game[/b]. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35734802/30d2a51333b351b6547ae0aa21e210e55d7222da.jpg[/img]

In what may be an industry first, Sky of Tides will feature an original animated series that will be available exclusively for a limited time and at no extra charge to players who beat the game. The five-episode [b]Sky of Tides: Atla[/b], which explores the Sky of Tides world Numen9 from the perspective of another protagonist, Atla Gildeon, will unlock inside the game for players who are able to complete the title’s stated goal of obtaining balance.

notes.title: This narrative led sci-fi RPG makes dialogue the star of the show
notes.notes:
We all love making dialogue choices in games. Whether it's choosing who to help in Fallout New Vegas, what variation of swear words to say in Baldur's Gate 3, or the colorful surprise thoughts of Disco Elysium, being offered multiple ways to talk yourself out of a situation instead of using violence is always fun. This is exactly what sci-fi narrative RPG Sky of Tides is going for, and you can try it ahead of a full launch right now.
